list_child.name: ls_batches
list_child.desc: Returns the full list of brew batches currently tracked in the production system. Use this when you need a complete overview of everything in progress or already packaged.

get_child.name: get_batch
get_child.desc: Retrieves a single brew batch record using its unique identifier. This is the way to pull up full detail on one batch instead of scanning the whole list.

list_parent.name: ls_accts
list_parent.desc: Returns every account the brewery currently sells or distributes to. This includes taprooms, restaurants, and retail partners on file.

get_parent.name: get_acct
get_parent.desc: Retrieves a single account record by its identifier. Use this when you already know which account you need and just want its details.

delete_child.name: kill_batch
delete_child.desc: Permanently deletes a brew batch record from the system, and this cannot be undone once it runs. Only use this for batches that were dumped, mislabeled, or never should have been logged.

set_enum.name: set_batch_state
set_enum.desc: Moves a brew batch to a new production state, covering brewing, fermenting, conditioning, or packaged. This is the standard way production status gets updated as a batch moves through the cellar.

set_bool.name: flag_recall
set_bool.desc: Marks a brew batch as under recall, pulling it out of normal circulation. This should only be used when there is a real quality or safety concern with the batch.

set_ref.name: move_acct
set_ref.desc: Reassigns a brew batch from one account to another, which is useful when an order gets transferred or a distributor relationship changes. The batch keeps its full history after the move.

send.name: call_acct
send.desc: Places a call to the contact on file for a given account. Use this when a batch needs a direct conversation instead of a written note.
